It seems that the assumption that `scorer` cannot be `null` is violated in some cases:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d2ef93dff175ba22406054bf78137679a0e7990c/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/aggregations/bucket/BestBucketsDeferringCollector.java#L167-L169

Thanks for reporting @BastianHofmann and thanks for investigating @danielmitterdorfer .
The NPE occurs because we expect that query and aggregation match the same document when we try to rebuild a scorer (breadth_first mode of the `terms` aggregation). This is not the case here since the `children` aggregator switches the context of the query to documents that don't necessarily match the parent query. This is not an issue when the score of documents is not needed but the `top_docs` aggregation accesses the `_score` by default to sort the hits. 
A simple workaround is to add a `sort` criteria to the `top_docs` aggregation:
````

"top_hits": {
  "sort": ["_doc"]
}
````

I don't know what is the expectation here but if the score of a child document should be equal to the score of its parent we would need to save each parent's score during the collection. Considering that this would require 4 bytes per document I don't think we should allow the `_score` to be used in a sub-aggregation of a `children` agg, it is too costly. Instead we could simply throw an error that explain why the score cannot be used.

@jimczi thank you for the provided workaround. This would certainly work for my use case, since I don't care which document is returned by the top_hits aggregation (all of the documents in the bucket will have the same user).
An error that explains why the score cannot be used would certainly be helpful.

issue.title: ParentJoinAggregator cannot have scoring sub-aggregators

issue.body:
It is generally expected that query and aggregation match the same document. This is not
the case with parent/children join aggregators, because they switch the context of the query
to documents so that they don't necessarily match the parent query. Therefore, we should not
allow sub-aggregations that use _score.

Closes #37650
